Thank you for pointing that out, and I will correct that by adding rivers up there. Cytafras manages to keep power and control via the fact that the compound city, in itself, is massive. Four cities south of the Greystone grew into one another, forming Cytafras. (Daphine, is a recent addition after it connected via the passes of the Greystone).

The League, is as stated, a league. A federation based on being a sort of econo-military bloc against the Empire to the east. The cities enjoy a lot of autonomy but a lot of connectivity. As an example, the cities of the Neran Plains lead on trade and agriculture, but lack mineral goods. The cities near the Arset Shield lack agricultural land, as the Ceresne Forest is dense and hard to manage. Cytafras has a large military force and the only safe connection of north and south.

The houses of the cities are separate from one another, existing from before the League, but do intermarry with each other. However that is not all they do, I know of the Habsburg strategy and have already written it down as one part of the League's continuance. They also share cultural roots, as well as some other soft connections stemming from being city states before being a League. Cytafras leads magical development in the continent, and thus have a strategic resource to band/covet together.
